title: fix(mcp): attribute phantom_fleet_needs_resolve to the agent surface, not Mason's CLI (post-merge #4761)
body:
Fix-forward from the Tier-1 post-merge security review of #4761.

**Finding (medium, authority attribution; not one of the four hard-limit categories):** `src/core/mcp-native.ts:497` (master 34ea67b8) passes `source: 'cli'` when the new MCP tool `phantom_fleet_needs_resolve` resolves a needs-you item. The bus event is written `from: 'mason'` with `source: 'cli'` (`src/core/fleet/needs-mason-resolve.ts:139-141`), and the MASON-INBOX relay is labeled `CLI` (`src/core/fleet/needs-mason-relay.ts:15`), which the planner reads as `[src:cli]`. Any MCP-connected agent could therefore record a needs-you answer that is indistinguishable from Mason's own CLI answer, including for parked approval items. The tool description says it is never permission, but nothing enforced or recorded that.

**Change:**
- `src/core/mcp-native.ts`: record `source: 'leader'` (already in the `NeedsMasonOptions['source']` union and within the 32-char `SOURCE_MAX` read by `needs-mason-answer.ts`).
- `src/core/fleet/needs-mason-relay.ts`: add `leader: 'Agent via MCP unverified'` so the inbox entry lands as `[src:agent-via-mcp-unverified]` instead of falling back to `Phantom desktop`.
- `test/mcp-native-fleet-needs-03-sopd1.test.ts`: assertions updated to the new attribution.

The envelope stays `from: 'mason'` because `needs-mason-answer.ts:86` only reads `from === 'mason'`; the body `source` now separates agent relays. Desktop, CLI, Telegram, phone and email paths are unchanged. Not run locally (review lane has no clone); affected tests are `test/mcp-native-fleet-needs-03-sopd1.test.ts`, `test/needs-reply-attribution.test.ts`, `test/needs-mason-reply-inbox.test.ts`.

title: bridge: RQ-PHX-DEVINFLEETMODEL89
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-PHX-DEVINFLEETMODEL89` (pool: devin), single commit on base `e19af3732`.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-PHX-DEVINFLEETMODEL89

The desktop Devin card (Resources drawer) now shows which model the fleet's
Devin lane launches with and whether it is a free promotional model. Read
only: nothing about which model runs, budgets, billing or plans changed.

## What changed

- `src/core/devin/cli-engine.ts` — additive pure helpers next to the existing
  model functions (no behavior change to them):
  - `devinCliFleetModelSource(section)` → `'config' | 'default'` — whether
    `devin.fleetModel` is the well-formed value the resolver reads.
  - `devinCliFleetModelPromo(model, nowMs)` → `'free' | 'not-free' |
    'unknown'` — 'free' only on `isDevinCliFreeModel`'s answer; 'not-free' on
    a `-lightning` id or after `DEVIN_CLI_PROMOTION_EVIDENCE_BOUNDARY`; else
    'unknown' (a pre-boundary id not on the free list is never claimed free).
  - `devinCliLaneModelEntries(lanes)` → sorted `{ key, model, paid }` rows
    for every resolved `devin*` models.json key; `paid` flags `-lightning`.
- `src/core/devin/types.ts` — new `DevinFleetModelInfo` and optional
  `fleetModel?: DevinFleetModelInfo | null` on `DevinOverviewResponse`.
- `src/core/devin/service.ts` — `devinOverview` now returns `fleetModel`:
  `configured` = `resolveDevinCliFleetModel(cfg.devin)`, `promo` at the
  overview's `now`, and `laneModels` via the existing
  `getLaneModelSnapshot` read of `~/.ashlr-runs/models.json` (new
  `DevinServiceDeps.laneModels` seam for tests). A missing, unreadable or
  failing snapshot yields `laneModels: []`, never an error.
- `src/web-ui/routes/verse/devin/devin-model.ts` — `devinFleetModelEvidence`
  (strict narrow of the optional field; null on older/malformed servers) and
  `devinFleetModelLines` ("Fleet model: <id> · free promo / not free / free
  status unknown" + one warning per paid models.json key).
- `src/web-ui/routes/verse/resources/DevinResource.tsx` — renders the
  fleet-model row with `data-devin-fleet-model` and a warning line per paid
  key ("models.json devin.fast = swe-2-max-lightning is a paid model; fleet
  runs fall back to swe-2-flash-max."). When `promo === 'free'` the dollar
  estimate gains "(fleet model is a free promo; estimate may not apply)".
  Old servers without the field render nothing new.

## Tests (new)

- `test/devin-overview-fleet-model.test.ts` — configured model + 'config'
  source; compiled default when unset; `-lightning` config resolves to
  swe-2-flash-max with promo `unknown` before and `not-free` after a fixed
  boundary clock; a free-list model is `free` before and `not-free` after;
  `devin*` keys read from a real temp models.json through
  `getLaneModelSnapshot` (the `devin.fast` `-lightning` entry flagged paid,
  non-devin keys excluded); missing/broken models.json and a throwing
  snapshot dep all yield `[]`. 5 tests.
- `src/web-ui/routes/verse/resources/DevinResource.fleetmodel.test.tsx` —
  free row + estimate caveat; not-free and unknown rows without the caveat;
  paid-lane warnings (two paid keys, free key not warned); absent and
  malformed field render nothing new. 5 tests.

## Commands run / results

- `npm run install:worktree` — the fresh worktree's node_modules was only
  partially materialized (eslint had no `lib/`, no `tsgo`); the pnpm shared
  store install + heal completed it.
- `npx eslint` on all 7 changed/new files: clean, 0 problems.
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/devin-overview-fleet-model.test.ts`
  — 5/5 pass.
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run --config vitest.config.web.ts
  src/web-ui/routes/verse/resources/DevinResource.fleetmodel.test.tsx` — 5/5.
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run --config vitest.config.web.ts
  src/web-ui/routes/verse/resources/DevinResource.test.tsx` — 52/52.
- Regression suites on the touched paths, one at a time:
  `test/devin-api-315.test.ts` 23/23, `test/devin-lane-315.test.ts` 153/153,
  `test/devin-cli-followups-315.test.ts` 10/10, `test/devin-cli-engine-315.test.ts` 42/42.
- `npx --no-install tsgo --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` — exit 0.
- `npx --no-install tsgo --noEmit -p src/web-ui/tsconfig.json` — exit 0.

## Notes / limits

- `laneModels` lists every `devin*` key a launch resolves to (the snapshot's
  `via`s). A `devin*` key fully shadowed by `devin.<tier>` keys for every
  tier never affects a launch and is not listed.
- `promo` describes the resolved model id only; it is `unknown` for any
  pre-boundary id outside `DEVIN_CLI_FREE_MODELS` and never asserts a live
  free route.
- Diff: 7 files, +136/−1 in tracked sources plus the two new test files;
  well under the 400-line bound. Not committed, per instructions.
</details>

Leader thread header now shows one line — "Dot: last text 4 min ago, answered"
or "Dot: last text 23 min ago, NOT answered" — urgent once an unanswered text
is 10+ minutes old, "Dot: no iMessage record yet" when there is no record, and
"Dot: reply status unknown" when the read is unavailable (never a faked time).

## Data source

`<runs>/imessage/teammates.jsonl`, read through `readRows` in
`src/core/comms/imessage-teammate-inbox.ts` — the same durable record the
unified inbox and `ashlr fleet teammate-texts` read. One `{v,at,rowid,senderId,
text}` line per allowlisted non-Mason inbound iMessage; one `{v,answered,at}`
marker per resolved text (teammate responder after a confirmed send or a
suppress, or Mason's desktop reply POST). No new poller, no chat.db reads.

`lastOutboundAt` is the answer-marker time of the NEWEST inbound text, so
`lastOutboundAt >= lastInboundAt` is exactly "the last text was answered" —
the client's formula and the server's flag can never disagree. Marker times
are resolution time (reply confirmed or suppressed), written by
`markTeammateTextsAnswered`. No HTTP endpoint previously exposed teammate
message times (comms/inbox lists unanswered texts only, without answer times),
so one was added.

  lastOutboundAt, answered}`. Mounted-module convention: 405 on non-GET, 404
  without allowDispatch, `source: 'unavailable'` + nulls on read failure.

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-PHX-INTENTPROVENANCEJOIN10SRX1

## Summary

Intent import reconciliation now preserves provenance completeness: when two
imported copies share one provenance identity (`source`/`date`/`verbatim`) but
differ only in `partial`, the stored row deterministically records
`partial: false` (a complete source copy was observed), regardless of import
order. Previously `addProvenance` deduped on the identity and kept whichever
`partial` value arrived first, so a truncated copy imported before a full copy
left weaker provenance on the ledger.

The item's aggregate `partial` flag is unchanged: `absorb` still ORs it, so an
item stays partial while any observed source copy is partial. Status,
closureProposal (stays local to the surviving item), id, owner, source, PR,
evidence and RQ handling are untouched. No schema or cap changes;
`MAX_PROVENANCE` slicing is preserved in both merge paths.

## Changed paths

- `src/core/intent/import.ts` (+30/-1)
  - `sameProvenance` identity predicate extracted.
  - `addProvenance`: on identity match, `partial: false` wins
    (`existing.partial && !row.partial → false`); otherwise append + cap as before.
  - `mergedProvenance`: same identity merge applied to a single incoming item's
    own provenance rows before a fresh item enters the ledger (native files can
    carry duplicate identities).
  - `place`: fresh items get `mergedProvenance(incoming.provenance)`.
- `test/intent-provenance-completeness-10srx1.test.ts` (new, 7 tests)

is partial, and PR/evidence/RQ/status/closureProposal metadata is preserved

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-PHX-LEADERPUSHRESTORE10SRU1

## Summary

Recovered the retained #4359 "Leader-thread push refresh" implementation onto
current master (origin/master `5b1c28033c7e606d593214b9a790987caf1cb8af`,
unchanged at finish). Source PR head verified: `c0ead287106508dfe14b9489f079e4d547af4cac`
(`git fetch origin pull/4359/head`). The PR's merge-base (`b5fb563d85`) is only
hours old and master had not touched the three shared files since, so the
api.ts / sse.ts / LeaderConversation.tsx hunks applied byte-clean; the four
new files were checked out from the PR head verbatim.

What it does: the Leader thread is written by other processes (leader tick,
Telegram, iMessage), so `src/core/web/leader-thread-watch.ts` holds one
refcounted `fs.watch` per thread directory (survives atomic rotation),
debounced (250 ms), with a 2 s stat-poll fallback when `fs.watch` is
unavailable. `api.ts` subscribes it only for SSE clients whose `topics`
include `leader-thread` and emits a timestamp-only `{ at }` invalidation —
never message bodies — over the existing authenticated `/api/events`. The
client (`src/web-ui/data/sse.ts`) gains a live-status signal plus the
`leader-thread` event name; `use-leader-thread-push.ts` refetches the
existing authenticated thread query on each event and on stream (re)open,
while `LeaderConversation` relaxes polling to a 30 s backstop only while the

   #<N>" type=pullrequests` for each of the three returned only the PR itself —
   none is superseded by an open or merged PR. None is #1487/#1488/#2444.

   `patch-diff.githubusercontent.com/raw/ashlrai/phantom/pull/4387.diff`).

"MergeGraph" panel on the Growth console, backed by a new pure module

time per lane from the local jobs ledger).

## TS error and root cause

`src/web-ui/routes/verse/growth/MergeGraph.tsx(10,37): error TS2345`

```
Argument of type '{ key: string; fetch: (signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<MergeGraphReport>; }'
is not assignable to parameter of type 'QueryDef<MergeGraphReport>'.
  Types of property 'fetch' are incompatible.
    Type '(signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<MergeGraphReport>' is not assignable to
    type '(signal?: AbortSignal | undefined) => Promise<MergeGraphReport>'.
```

Root cause: signature drift against current master. `QueryDef.fetch` (in
`src/web-ui/data/queries.ts`) is `(signal?: AbortSignal) => Promise<T>` — the
cache calls `def.fetch()` with no argument — but the PR declared its fetch as
`(signal: AbortSignal)` with a required parameter, which fails
`strictFunctionTypes`.

Fix: made the parameter optional — `fetch: (signal?: AbortSignal) => apiGet<MergeGraphReport>(...)`,
matching every other `QueryDef` in `src/web-ui/data/queries.ts` and
`apiGet(path, signal?)` which already accepts `signal?: AbortSignal`. No `any`,
no ts-ignore.

of its per-file diffs, not a whole-branch copy):

body:

**Tests:** no test command

**Tier-1 (CODEOWNERS) paths, async post-merge review:** .github/scripts/ci-pack-smoke.mjs .github/scripts/release-fast-smoke.mjs .github/tests/ci-pack-smoke.test.mjs .github/tests/ci-release-same-runner.test.mjs .github/tests/release-isolated-tree.test.mjs .github/workflows/ci.yml .github/workflows/release-desktop.yml scripts/build-outputs.mjs scripts/release-isolated-tree.mjs scripts/release-smoke-timing.mjs test/config/realio-lane-membership.mjs

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES: RQ-PHX-RECUTR2000S73

Recut of **#2880 "bridge: RQ-NODE-4-VIEW"**. Commit subject: `bridge(RQ-NODE-4-VIEW): BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-NODE-4-VIEW`, own commit `b4f858e4e2`. It is the oldest open PR in 2000-2999 whose work is still missing from master.

Closes #2880

## How the candidates were found

`gh` could not run in this sandbox: reading `~/.config/gh/config.yml` returns "operation not permitted", and the unauthenticated REST API was rate-limited (403). I did not pull credentials out of the keychain to get around that. Instead:

1. `git fetch origin '+refs/pull/2*/head:refs/rq2000/pr/2*'` fetched the head of every PR numbered 2000-2999.
2. I dropped any PR whose number appears as `(#N)` in a master commit subject, or whose `bridge(<JOB>)` id appears in one. Those are squash-merged or already recut. That left 77.
3. For those 77 I read the state from the public PR page (`"state":"OPEN|CLOSED|MERGED"`): 63 closed, 1 merged, 13 open. #2923 is also open: it is the only PR in range with a `refs/pull/N/merge` ref, and its job id is on master.
4. Master is now a single squashed commit, so each PR's own work is its tip non-merge commit diffed against its parent. Whole-branch diffs would drag in the rewritten history.

## Candidates checked, oldest first

| PR | Job | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| #2774 | RQ-PHX-SAFARIIMPORTVERB01 | superseded | `src/cli/fleet-safari-import.ts`, `src/cli/fleet-app.ts`, `test/fleet-app-verb-01.test.ts` and the python ingress files are on master. Registry lines `'app'`, `'safari-import'` and `'session'` are on master (lines 8, 317, 325). The script runner was recut as `safari-import-helper.ts` (`test/fleet-safari-import-helper-recutolda60.test.ts`). |
| #2831 | RQ-DRAIN-phantom-1019 | skipped | RQ-DRAIN filler |
| #2837 | RQ-GUARDIANHEADQ8 | superseded by content | `guardian-head-manifest.ts` and the `--head-of` flag are missing, but `ashlr fleet guardian-manifest --repo R --branch origin/<b> --limit 1 --out F` followed by `guardian-verify --manifest F` builds the same one-entry head and first-parent manifest. Master's `guardianManifestEntries` also binds two-parent merges correctly (candidate = parent 2), which #2837's version does not. Recutting it would add a second, weaker manifest builder. |
| #2842 | RQ-DRAIN-phantom-1110 | skipped | RQ-DRAIN filler |
| #2850 | RQ-NODE-1-JOIN | superseded | `phm node join|status|leave` are on master through the node router: `src/cli/node-fleet-usage.ts` `NODE_FLEET_VERBS`, `docs/NODES.md`, `docs/add-a-computer.md`. |
| **#2880** | **RQ-NODE-4-VIEW** | **recut (web half missing)** | The CLI half is on master as `ashlr fleet nodes` (`src/cli/fleet-nodes.ts`, `buildNodesSnapshot` in `src/core/nodes/view.ts`). The web half is not: `git grep '/api/nodes\|NodesPanel' origin/master` finds nothing, and `NodesPanel.tsx` is absent. |
| #2923 | RQ-PHX-MCPSELFTICKLAST02 | superseded | `fleet_self_tick_last` and `src/mcp/fleet-self-tick.ts` are on master, recut as RQ-PHX-DIRTYPHXRECUT57 (#4579). |

I stopped at the first real gap, #2880. Still open and not checked against master: #2884, #2888, #2906, #2910, #2915, #2936 and #2960. #2906, #2936 and #2960 are FIXUP-MAIN web typecheck fixups.

## Files taken (adapted to master's evolved snapshot)

- `src/core/web/api.ts`: added the `GET /api/nodes` route, which serves `buildNodesSnapshot()` (no-auth read class, like `/api/control`). I also fixed a bug the new route test exposed: `sendJson` turned **any** `error` key into a string, so a healthy snapshot's `error: null` arrived as `"null"`, and the panel would have shown a false alert. Bounding now applies only to a non-null `error`. Nothing relied on the old coercion; the m14 API and universe web API suites still pass.
- `src/core/nodes/view.ts`: added `export type NodesSnapshot = ReturnType<typeof buildNodesSnapshot>` so the panel can type its query. Existing exported signatures are unchanged.
- `src/web-ui/routes/fleet-dashboard/NodesPanel.tsx` (new), adapted from the PR:
  - It reads master's `error` field; the PR's `problems[]` does not exist on master.
  - Recovery hints say `ashlr fleet nodes` instead of the never-landed `phm nodes`.
  - It polls through `usePollWhileVisible`, like `ResourcePanel`, instead of a raw `setInterval`.
  - It pins tones for ready, stale and down, which the shared map would render as neutral.
  - It adds an empty-inventory hint (`phm node join`).
- `src/web-ui/routes/fleet-dashboard/NodesPanel.module.css` (new, unchanged from the PR).
- `src/web-ui/routes/fleet-dashboard/NodesPanel.test.tsx` (the PR's own test, adapted to master's shape, 4 cases).
- `src/web-ui/routes/fleet-dashboard/FleetDashboardView.tsx`: mounts `<NodesPanel />` after `<ResourcePanel />`.

## Files dropped

- `src/cli/nodes.ts`, plus its hunks in `src/cli/index.ts`, `src/cli/help.ts` and `src/cli/completions.ts`: superseded by `ashlr fleet nodes`. A second top-level `phm nodes` verb would duplicate it.
- `src/core/nodes/view.ts` (the PR's whole-file version) and `src/core/nodes/age.ts`: master has evolved versions that read the router's `nodes.json`. I kept master's and only added the type export.
- `test/nodes-view.test.ts` and `test/fixtures/nodes/*.json`: they test the PR's per-file registry model and `cmdNodes`, neither of which exists on master. `test/fleet-nodes-reconcile-09snu2.test.ts` covers master's equivalent.
- `docs/README.md`: off-limits to this job.
- `docs/NODES-VIEW.md`, `AGENTS.md` and `llms.txt`: they document the dropped `phm nodes` verb, which `test/doc-facts.test.ts` would reject.
- `~/.npm/_update-notifier-last-checked`: junk file the PR committed by accident.

## Diff size

`git diff --stat origin/master` (master `9680d22d44`, new files included): **7 files**, +262 / -1. With this note it is 8, under the limit of 22 (#2880's 20 files + 2). Net LOC: +261.

I re-fetched master just before finishing. None of the touched shared files (`api.ts`, `view.ts`, `FleetDashboardView.tsx`) changed between the base and the newest master, and the worktree is fast-forwarded to `9680d22d44`.

## Commands and results

- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/recut-range-2000-2999.test.ts test/fleet-nodes-reconcile-09snu2.test.ts test/web-host-summary.test.ts`: 3 files, **27/27 passed**.
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/m14.api.test.ts test/universe-web-api.test.ts` (regression check for the `sendJson` change): 2 files, **48/48 passed**.
- `npx vitest run --config vitest.config.web.ts src/web-ui/routes/fleet-dashboard/`: 3 files, **7/7 passed** (NodesPanel, FleetDashboardView, ResourcePanel).
- `npx eslint` on the 6 changed TS/TSX files: **0 problems**. The worktree's `node_modules/eslint` had no `lib/` directory; I restored it from an identical eslint@9.39.5 install in a temp dir. That copy is gitignored and belongs to this worktree only.
- `test/recut-range-2000-2999.test.ts` drives the real `handleApi` route. It checks the leader, roles, stale and ready status, live jobs, caps and auth from a temp `ASHLR_HOME` router inventory. It also checks that a missing inventory returns 200 with `error: "inventory missing"`, that a fake token-shaped cap is refused without being echoed, and that `POST /api/nodes` gets a 404.

## Typecheck

tsgo is not installed in this worktree, so the fallback ran in the foreground, one at a time:

- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json --incremental false`: **exit 0**, 0 errors, 262 s.
- `tsconfig.json` excludes `src/web-ui`, so the NodesPanel types were checked separately afterwards: `npx tsc --noEmit -p src/web-ui/tsconfig.json --incremental false` gave **exit 0**, 0 errors. No source changed after either run.

No commits, pushes or secrets. `~/.codex` was not touched.
</details>

- Oldest candidate **#3306: work missing, not superseded.**

  `test/recut-range-3300-3599.test.ts` rather than in a separate file, which
  keeps the diff within the file cap.

Dropped:
- `test/m31.native-tools.test.ts` hunk. On master that test no longer
  hard-codes tool names; it derives them from `docs/MCP-TOOLS.md` through
  `test/helpers/native-tool-contract.ts`.

Required by current master (the native-tool registration contract that came after the PR):
- `docs/MCP-TOOLS.md`: one table row. It is the contracted tool list.
- `test/mcp-output-efficiency.test.ts`: classifies the tool as an addition, gives it

```
HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/recut-range-3300-3599.test.ts \
```

Result: 6 files passed, 142 tests passed, 0 failed.

The recut test goes through the real entry points: `callNativeTool`,

`npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json --incremental false`, which **exited 0**.

## Final master check
Just before finishing I re-fetched origin master: 0 new commits since the base.
None of the touched shared files had drifted.

Closes #3306

body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-PHX-SLACKSTATUSROUNDTRIP10` (pool: claude), single commit on base `67732c188`.

**Tests:** no test command

**Tier-1 (CODEOWNERS) paths, async post-merge review:** test/fixtures/authority/tier1-closure.json test/wb-read-api.test.ts

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# RQ-PHX-SLACKSTATUSROUNDTRIP10: Slack "Phantom status" round trip

Base: origin/master 155ebde0f (worktree fast-forwarded to it before any edit; re-fetched at the end, unchanged).

## Hop trace (before this change), one inbound "Phantom status" from the verified operator

1. `src/cli/channels-slack.ts:cmdSlackTransport`: opens the socket with `createSlackLeaderAdapter({ call, signal, statusReply: ownerStatusReply() })`. The fast path was already wired here.
2. `src/core/agents/slack-transport.ts:openSlackSocket` (message handler): `unwrapSlackSocketEnvelope`, then `leaderAdapter.normalize`.
3. `src/core/agents/slack-inbound.ts:slackEventToBus`: team, channel map, allowlist and loop guard. Returns the `ingest` envelope (`channel: 'slack'`, thread ref `slack:<team>:<channel>:<thread_ts>`).
4. `src/core/agents/slack-leader.ts:createSlackLeaderAdapter.route` → `ingestSlackLeaderEnvelope`: verifies the operator id against `[mason]`, checks the Slack policy and calls `users.info` to prove the sender is a human.
5. `src/core/agents/leader-network.ts:createLeaderNetwork().ingest` → `appendInbox`. For Slack this goes through `options.appendInbox`.
6. `src/core/agents/leader-network-runtime.ts:leaderInboxAppender` → `src/core/agents/leader-inbox-writer.ts:approvedLeaderInboxAppender` → execFile `~/.ashlr-runs/bin/mason-inbox-append` (repo copy `contrib/mac/mason-inbox-append:record`). This writes `## <date> ET (Operator, slack) PRIORITY P0 [request-sha256:…] [leader-network:…]`. **(b) The MASON-INBOX write.**
7. `leader-network.ts:ingest` → `publish` (bus mirror of the ask).
8. Back in `ingestSlackLeaderEnvelope`, only after ingest returned `accepted`: `statusReply.ask` (`src/core/agents/owner-status-reply.ts:isOwnerStatusRequest`) → detached `composeOwnerStatusReply` (uses `leaderDailyBrief`) → `network.reply` → `deliverSlackLeaderMessage` → `slack-transport.ts:deliverSlackEnvelope` → `chat.postMessage` with `thread_ts`. **(a) The same-thread reply.**
9. `leader-runtime:noteUnifiedOwner` → unified owner thread receipt. The socket acks only when the route reports durable.

## Missing link

The fast path existed (SLACKSTATUS* jobs) and was called from the inbound path, but in the wrong order. Hop 8 runs only after hop 6 has already written the P0 order, so every status ask became a P0 inbox order whether or not it was answered. The answer was also fire-and-forget with no outcome, so an inbox entry could not be made to depend on it. In addition, the reply was gated on `accepted`, which required the sole-writer append to succeed first. A failed or slow `mason-inbox-append` (missing host helper, scrub refusal, 25s timeout) meant `unavailable` and no answer at all. That matches Mason's 11-06 messages: P0 entries, and no reply in Slack.

## What changed

`src/core/agents/slack-leader.ts`, `ingestSlackLeaderEnvelope` (the module that owns the inbox decision):
- **Pure status ask from the verified operator** (existing `isOwnerStatusRequest`; no new classifier): the ask is ingested with `inboxAlreadyRecorded: true`. The route stays durable and bus-published, which keeps replay dedupe, the Leader's pending queue and the socket ack, but nothing is written to MASON-INBOX. The answer comes from the existing `statusReply.compose` (`composeOwnerStatusReply` / `leaderDailyBrief`) and goes out through the existing journaled `network.reply`: MASON-OUTBOX record, a bus `leader-reply` (this is the bus log of the answer) and a `chat.postMessage` in the same thread.
- **Inbox:** the writer (`mason-inbox-append`) has no non-priority Slack format, so per the spec the inbox write is skipped and the answer is logged to the bus and OUTBOX through the existing APIs.
- **Fallback:** if the reply is not `sent`/`duplicate` (Slack throws, transport or policy not configured at send, reply refused, bus unavailable) or the ask never reached the bus, the exact request the network would have sent (same requestId, receivedAt, text) goes to the same sole writer. That produces today's P0 block. A `console.warn` line says why (`status ask not answered in-thread (<reason>); recorded it in MASON-INBOX as P0 instead`). If the fallback write also fails, the line says so and the route stays pending for the Leader.
- **The fast path runs only when a sole-writer appender exists.** That is always the case on the installed host (`~/.ashlr-runs`) and whenever a trusted `appendInbox` seam is injected. In isolated custom roots with no appender there would be no fallback writer, so status asks there take the ordinary path (P0, no auto answer) instead of risking a dropped ask.
- The answer runs detached, as before, so the socket ack is not held. `ingestSlackLeaderEnvelope` now also returns `statusAnswer?: Promise<SlackStatusAnswer>` (new exported type `{ answered, reason }`) so callers and tests can observe the outcome. Nothing else changed in the signature. It is not listed in CONTRACT.md or docs/contracts.
- Removed the old detached-only block (its compose/timeout logic moved into `answerOwnerStatus`) and the duplicate body-text extraction.
- Unchanged: non-status messages (P0 as today), non-operator senders (not owned, no answer, no inbox write), and the verification order (`[mason]` id, team policy, `users.info` human proof). An allowed `[team]` sender is never treated as the operator.

## Tests

- NEW `test/slack-status-roundtrip.test.ts` (213 lines) drives the real `openSlackSocket` → `slackEventToBus` → `ingestSlackLeaderEnvelope` → Leader network → `deliverSlackEnvelope` path. It uses a fake Slack transport, a temp-dir inbox writer and synthetic ids (U000FAKEOPERATOR, C000FAKECHANNEL). Cases:
  - "Phantom status": exactly one post in the same thread, text from the existing builder, no P0 block, the answer present in OUTBOX and on the bus; a redelivery neither re-answers nor writes.
  - "status?", "What's the status" and "STATUS!" behave the same.
  - "status of release, then cut 3.30.32": a P0 block and no answer.
  - A non-operator sender: unchanged.
  - Slack send throws: a P0 block plus the warn line.
  - Transport not configured at send time: a P0 block.
  - darwin only: the fallback runs through the real `contrib/mac/mason-inbox-append` in a private fixture and the exact `PRIORITY P0 [request-sha256:…]` heading is asserted.
  - `isOwnerStatusRequest` accept and reject cases.
- UPDATED `test/slack-leader-status-reply.test.ts`: it now injects a temp-dir sole-writer stand-in, because the fast path requires a fallback writer. The first case's assertion changed from "still records the ask in the inbox" to "no P0 order in the inbox", which is the behavior this job asks for. The post-failure case now asserts the P0 fallback entry. No case was removed or skipped.

## Commands run

- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/slack-status-roundtrip.test.ts`: 23/23 pass.
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/slack-leader-status-reply.test.ts`: 5/5 pass.
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/owner-status-reply.test.ts`: 29/29 pass.
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/slack-leader.test.ts`: 10/10 in 3 of 4 runs with this change. This suite is flaky on pristine origin/master too: with the master `slack-leader.ts` restored it failed in 3 of 4 runs (`expected "vi.fn()" to be called once` / 5000 ms per-case deadline). The flake is pre-existing and not caused by this change.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json --incremental false` (tsgo is not installed here): exit 0. A temporary in-repo tsconfig that included the two test files also showed no errors in them; it was deleted afterwards.
- `npx eslint <changed files>`: **could not run.** The worktree's `node_modules/eslint` has no `lib/` directory (`Cannot find module '../lib/cli'`), and `npx -p eslint@9.39.5` resolves to the same broken local copy. Lint is not verified; repairing it needs `npm ci`.
- `git fetch origin master`: HEAD == origin/master 155ebde0f, so the change applies cleanly. `git diff --stat`: 2 tracked files changed plus 1 new test file plus this notes file (4 files).

## Net LOC

`src/core/agents/slack-leader.ts` +53/−21 (net +32), `test/slack-leader-status-reply.test.ts` +19/−6, `test/slack-status-roundtrip.test.ts` +213 (new).
</details>

# RQ-PHX-RECUTEVEN62: recut of #2928 (RQ-PHX-SELFLOOPSTOPFILE02SOLD2)

Supersedes #2928

## Summary

Recovered `ashlr fleet self-loop --stop-file <abs>`: an operator or supervisor
stop file that ends admission gracefully. The PR was stranded on a stale base.
- If the file already exists, no pass runs (termination `stop-file`, exit 0).
- If the file is created during the idle wait, admission stops promptly. An
  event-driven watch on the parent directory races the sleep; there is no polling.
- If the file is created mid-pass, that pass finishes and no further pass runs.
- A missing file leaves repetition unchanged. The file is only read, never
  created or removed.
- Any filesystem error other than ENOENT ends the run as `stop-check-error`,
  exit 1. It never keeps launching passes blind.
- Relative, empty, missing, duplicate or control-character values exit 2
  before any pass.
- Human output labels: `STOPPED-BY-FILE` and `STOP-CHECK-ERROR`.

Master's self-loop has moved on since #2928 (it now has max-ticks, failure and
busy backoff, pre-abort and deadline-capped sleeps). I re-applied the hunks by
hand onto that newer code instead of taking the PR file.

One fix beyond the PR: when the stop watch wins the race against the
inter-tick sleep, the losing sleep is now aborted through a per-wait
`AbortController` linked to the run signal. Before this, a real
`sleepCancellable` timer stayed armed and could keep the process alive for up
to one interval after the summary printed. It only applies when a stop seam
is wired, so behaviour without `--stop-file` is byte-identical. A new test
covers it.

  on `~/.config/gh/config.yml`), so I listed open PRs through the
  unauthenticated public REST API (`/repos/ashlrai/phantom/pulls?state=open`,
  326 open). Even-numbered `codex-bridge/RQ-PHX-*` PRs, oldest first: #2774,
  #2912, #2928, #2966, ... None are on the skip list.

  sits on a stale merge-base well behind master, so I treated them as
  DIRTY/BEHIND.

  `src/cli/fleet-app.ts` and `scripts/mac-bridge/test_host_queue_ingress_lanes.py`
  exist on master. The `header_lane`/`--lane`/`filtered` hunks are in
  `scripts/mac-bridge/host_queue_ingress.py` (lines 64, 82, 105, 150). The
  registry has `safari-import` and `app`. Safari import was recut earlier as
  the helper version (`test/fleet-safari-import-helper-recutolda60.test.ts`).
- **#2912 CHANGELOGFRAGMENTS02: skipped as update/release flow** (owned by
  RQ-PHX-RECUTRELEASE61). `fleet-changelog.ts` and `changelog-fold.ts` are
  missing on master. The fold targets a `## [x.y.z] — Unreleased` heading,
  but master's CHANGELOG.md uses `## [Unreleased]` maintained by
  `scripts/changelog-sync.mjs` and release-please. Its other 51 files are

Supersedes #4469. Every file and hunk of that PR is in this change, so #4469 can be closed once this lands.

## What it does
The Fleet host pane in the desktop/web app gets a **Disk forecast** card. It reads a new
read-only route, `GET /api/verse/fleet/memory/disk-forecast`, which runs the existing
`diskForecast()` (`src/core/fleet/disk-forecast.ts`, already on master behind
`phm fleet disk-forecast`) over `<runs>/queue/disk-growth-history.json` and
`<runs>/metrics/jobs.jsonl`. Example output: "Free disk reaches 150 GB in about 9 h (Tue 03:10) at 4.2 GB/h".
- Missing, unreadable or too-short history shows "Disk trend unknown: not enough samples"
  with "0 samples · window unknown". The card never shows a guessed number.
- A read error in the route returns `status: 'unknown'`. Non-GET returns 405. Nothing is cleaned up or changed on disk.
- If the route is missing on an older backend (404), the card renders nothing.
- Tone thresholds: under 6 h is bad, under 24 h is warn, otherwise neutral. Unknown is neutral, with no tone styling.

title: bridge: RQ-PHOS-2-REGISTRY
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-PHOS-2-REGISTRY` (pool: claude), single commit on base `5b52c782f`.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-PHOS-2-REGISTRY

Capability registry and adapter generator (PHANTOM-OS-1, PR 1). Uncommitted in
the worktree, as instructed. Branch for the PR: `feature/RQ-PHOS-2-REGISTRY`.
It goes through the merge queue; do not self-merge.

## Summary

- **Schema** (`src/core/caps/schema.ts`, Zod, `caps.registry.v1`): surfaces,
  models, hosting edges, sessions, account references, egress allowlists and
  capabilities (mcp / skill / plugin / cli / connector). All objects are
  closed.
- **Loader and validator** (`src/core/caps/registry.ts`):
  - Screens the raw document for secret-shaped text before parsing, so no
    diagnostic can echo a value.
  - Checks cross-references and anchors on the existing router. Surface
    `engine` must exist in `run/engine-registry.ts`. Model `catalogId` must be
    in `KNOWN_MODELS`, and `providerModelId` must match that catalog entry. No
    second source of truth.
  - Router queries: `resolveSurfaceModelPair` (same lane only, with the host
    path in `via`), `surfaceModelPairs`, `hostedSurfaces`,
    `gatedCapabilities`.
- **Surfaces vs models**: they are distinct record types, and an id cannot
  name both. Fable 5.2 is a `claude`-lane model (family `claude-fable`,
  allowance `claude-max-weekly-fable`), not a surface. The Weyv lead is a
  session: Claude Code pinned to `claude-fable-5-2`. Devin CLI and Devin
  Desktop host GLM Lite, Cursor, Grok Build, Gemini, Copilot, Qwen and Codex
  through first-class `hosting` edges. Validation rejects cycles,
  self-hosting, duplicate edges and orphan hosted-only surfaces.
- **Security rules enforced**:
  - (a) Control-backend allowlist. `tcc-db`, `tcc-grant`, `app-db`, `scrape`
    and `screen-scrape` are refused by name. CDP/Playwright needs a per-run
    profile and 127.0.0.1.
  - (b) Accounts hold a credential name, store and scopes only.
  - (c) Local runtimes need `bind: 127.0.0.1`, `keyForwarding: false` and a
    defined egress allowlist reference.
  - (d) `external_send`, `spend` and `delete` are required booleans. Effects
    imply flags, and each flag requires its gate (`outside-send`, `money`,
    `destroy-data`; ids from `HardLimit`).
  - (e) Outputs are pinned (see below).
  - (f) `autoFile.fields` is a closed enum with no field for screen contents
    or secrets.
- **Adapter generator** (`src/core/caps/generate.ts`): deterministic output
  for Claude Code and Desktop, Fable sessions, Codex (TOML), Devin (with one
  `hosted[]` sub-config per guest), Cursor, Grok Build, Gemini, Copilot and
  local models.
  - Credentials appear only as host-expanded references.
  - Gated capabilities are never loaded directly. They are listed in the
    manifest `gated` and denied in Claude Code settings.
  - Each artifact has a sha256. `SHA256SUMS` is in `sha256sum` format,
    `bundleSha256` is the sha of that file, and the manifest has a `pinStage`
    block (SEC-PIN-STAGE-TOOL-2, `pin_stage_lib` fe77a6a8, staged dir
    `~/.ashlr-runs/staged/caps/<bundleSha256>`). Phantom does not invoke the
    tool and does not edit pinned bin/ files.
- **Output guard** (`src/core/caps/output.ts`): allowlist roots only (a
  worktree subdirectory, or `~/.ashlr-runs/staged/`).
  - Refuses `~/.codex`, `~/.claude`, `~/.cursor`, `~/.gemini`, `~/.devin`,
    `~/.config`, `~/Library` and similar.
  - Refuses repo-local live paths (`.claude/`, `.cursor/`, `.vscode/`,
    `.mcp.json`).
  - Resolves symlinks first.
  - Removes only stale files listed in its own previous manifest.
- **CLI**: `phm caps list|validate|generate [--registry] [--out] [--pin-stage]
  [--check] [--json]`. The handler `src/cli/caps.ts` is thin; the logic is in
  `src/core/caps/service.ts`. It is registered in `index.ts`,
  `completions.ts`, `help.ts`, the README command table, `docs/cli.md`,
  `docs/CLI-REFERENCE.md`, `docs/llms.txt` and `docs/CODEMAP.md`.
- **Data**:
  - `capabilities/registry.v1.json`: 16 surfaces, 11 models, 14 hosting
    edges, 1 session, 5 accounts, 15 capabilities, 20 routable pairs.
  - Committed generated output in `capabilities/generated/`. A test enforces
    zero drift, and another test enforces that the companion MCP launch specs
    match `.mcp.json`.
- **Docs**: `docs/CAPABILITY-REGISTRY.md`.
- **Pre-existing drift fixed in passing** (these drift tests were red on
  master because of #4618 and an earlier `constitution` add):
  - Registered `constitution` and `wb` in completions.
  - Added a `wb` help entry and `check`, `constitution` and `wb` README rows.
  - `phm wb --help` now prints usage and exits 0, as the repo's help rule
    requires.

## Decisions worth a look

- `launch.env` is a list of `{ name, account }`, not a `NAME -> id` map. The
  shared secret scrubber correctly reads `"X_API_KEY": "id"` as an assignment,
  so the shape changed rather than the screen.
- The output re-screen masks only the generator's own sha256 digests, which
  are 64-hex strings the scrubber would otherwise flag.
- The registry is not added to the published package `files` allowlist. That
  list is reviewed (m454/m482). `phm caps` is a checkout tool and says so when
  run elsewhere.
- No Slack MCP package was invented. `slack-post`, `mail-send` and
  `messages-send` are gated connectors.
- Models with unknown provider ids are not recorded: Gemini, Copilot, Cursor
  and hosted Qwen have surfaces but no model entries yet. They can be added
  once the ids are verified.
- The Fable 5.2 catalog entry is `explicitOnly` / `seatRouted`. The Weyv
  session adapter is a staged artifact only and is not installed anywhere.

## Commands run (HOME set to a fresh mktemp dir each time)

- `npm run dev -- caps validate` → PASS
- `npm run dev -- caps generate` → 19 files, then `generate --check` → PASS
- `shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS` in `capabilities/generated` → all OK
- `npx vitest run test/caps-registry.test.ts test/cli-registry-drift.test.ts test/readme-command-table.test.ts test/cli-docs-drift.test.ts test/codemap-drift.test.ts test/doc-facts.test.ts`
  → 6 files, 73/73 passed. `caps-registry.test.ts` alone has 49 tests.
- `node scripts/verify-changed.mjs` (once, foreground) → exit 0:
  - tsc PASS
  - authority drift PASS (10/10)
  - realio lint PASS
  - verse sync-I/O lint PASS
  - ESLint SKIPPED: `node_modules/eslint/lib/cli.js` is absent in this
    environment (and broken in the main checkout too). Merge Gate lints on CI.
- `node scripts/docs-sync.mjs`. Unrelated version-pin freshness edits it made
  were reverted: `docs/QUICKSTART.md`, `examples/quickstart.md`,
  `site/llms-full.txt`.
- `npx vitest run test/cli-help-no-side-effects.test.ts` → 1263 passed and
  11 failed. All 11 failures are SIGKILL timeouts in commands this change
  does not touch (`comms-agent` ×5, `connectors` ×2, `radar` ×4), on a host
  running about 22 concurrent jobs. A targeted re-run with `-t` matched no
  tests, so these were not reproduced in isolation.
- Direct help check with a scratch HOME: `caps --help`, `caps -h`,
  `caps list|validate|generate --help`, `wb --help` and `wb -h` all exit 0
  and write nothing besides npx's own `.npm` cache.

## Net LOC

38 files, +3291 / −5. About 1,165 lines are source (`src/core/caps` and
`src/cli/caps.ts`). About 1,180 are generated pinned adapters plus their
manifest, 555 are tests and fixtures, and the rest is the registry data and
docs.
</details>

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-DESK-7-EVENTS (WB-8)

## Summary

Added `GET /api/wb/v1/events`, the workbench Server-Sent Events surface for
the desktop native shell, in the new module `src/core/web/wb-events.ts`.

Two event families share one stream:

- **`wb.*` kinds** — `wb.snapshot`, `wb.gh`, `wb.action` envelopes conforming
  to `schema/workbench.v1/event.schema.json` (`{schema, kind, ts, seq, repo?,
  audit?}`). `wb.snapshot`/`wb.gh` are invalidation signals emitted when their
  read projections change (sha256 digest-compared each tick; volatile
  `ageMs`/`stale`/`backoff` freshness metadata is excluded so timers never
  spam events). `wb.action` has no poll source — in-process producers publish
  it via `publishWbEvent()`. Envelopes are schema-shaped on emit: `repo` must
  match the schema's ashlrai-org pattern and `audit` must be an object, else
  the field is dropped rather than emitting an invalid frame.
- **`queue.v1` relay** — relays RQ-QUEUE-2 station events from the private
  journal at `~/.ashlr/telemetry/router-queue/events.json` (the path
  `phm telemetry queue` writes per docs/ROUTER-QUEUE-STATIONS.md @ 8d13405).
  Events present at connect are baseline (not replayed); new events emit once
  each as `event: queue.v1` frames with `id:` = eventId for Last-Event-ID
  dedupe, plus an in-memory seen-set. Station events are strictly
  shape-validated against the real contract (station↔source attestation
  pairs, exact per-station evidence keys, canonical UTC-ms timestamps,
  64-hex eventIds); off-contract entries are dropped individually. A missing,
  oversized, symlinked, or malformed journal silences only the relay — the
  stream stays alive.

Security/durability properties:

- Same read-session boundary as every `/api/*` GET, plus the SSE convention:
  the route itself requires a minted read session (`SESSION_REQUIRED` on bare
  token auth), honors session expiry, and is admitted to the `?client=`
  query-proof path list in `read-session.ts`.
- Every emitted byte passes through `sanitizePublicJson` — secret-shaped
  strings become `[REDACTED]`, this user's home paths become `~`.
- Shares the `/api/events` connection cap and drain registry
  (`registerSse`/`deregisterSse`/`sseConnectionCapReached`); bounded poll
  cadence (2 s), keepalive (15 s), per-tick relay cap (200), seen-set cap
  (20k), write-buffer cap (4 MiB), stat-gated journal reads (mtime+size
  signature — unchanged files are never re-parsed).
- **No polling of Mac-dispatcher paths**: the only queue source is the
  `~/.ashlr` journal above; `~/.ashlr-runs` and `queue.v1.json` are never
  touched (asserted by test).
- RQ-QUEUE-2 has not landed on this base; the relay reads its documented
  on-disk contract. Until the journal exists the relay is simply silent.

## Files changed

- `src/core/web/wb-events.ts` — new (554 lines): SSE handler, wb.* envelope
  emission, `publishWbEvent`, queue.v1 journal reader/relay.
- `src/core/web/wb-read-api.ts` — route dispatch for `/api/wb/v1/events`
  (GET-only, session-required), `WbApiDeps`, exported `readWbSnapshot`,
  `WbGhDeps`.
- `src/core/web/api.ts` — pass `ctx.readSession` into `handleWbApi`.
- `src/core/web/read-session.ts` — admit `/api/wb/v1/events` to SSE
  query-proof auth.
- `src/cli/serve.ts` — `phm serve` help line for the new route.
- `test/wb-read-api.test.ts` — +336 lines: 13 new tests (auth boundary,
  schema-valid wb.* envelopes, change re-emission, `publishWbEvent`,
  queue.v1 relay/dedupe/baseline/malformed-journal/off-contract-drop,
  redaction, path discipline). Tests live here rather than a new file so no
  new Tier-1 test needs a `.github/CODEOWNERS` line (task: no .github).
- `test/fixtures/authority/tier1-closure.json` — regenerated (+1:
  `src/core/web/wb-events.ts` joined the Tier-1 import closure via
  `api.ts → wb-read-api.ts → wb-events.ts`; sanctioned snapshot update, not
  a .github change).

  test/workbench-schema.test.ts test/m14.api.test.ts
  test/m213.dashboard-sse.test.ts test/m503.dashboard-read-auth.test.ts
  test/perf-server-sse.test.ts test/web-console-sse-backpressure.test.ts`

lane is held, before it plans releases. Before this, a held `claude` lane waited

`claude` binary or a probe that throws gives `unavailable` and writes nothing.

body:

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-PHX-INTENTNATIVEEVIDENCE09SQN1

## Summary

Recovered PR #4235's native MCP intent evidence capabilities — `intent_stale`,
`intent_link` and `intent_ship` — onto current master contracts. Agents can now
inspect stale directives and persist explicitly supplied merge/release tracking
through the real native gateway (`tools/list` + `callNativeTool`). This is a
subset recovery of original work, not a new dashboard or release publisher;
#4235 is not closed by this change.

- Original source SHA inspected: `80f1d451949b26685cafa3ffa973d3933901634d`
  (`git fetch origin pull/4235/head`; FETCH_HEAD matched exactly).
- Base: `origin/master` `9189dc3d88`; re-fetched before finishing — master moved
  to `f19e1521e6` (release-train fix, bridge notes, intent-preservation doc
  refresh). None of the three commits touched `src/core/mcp-native.ts`,
  `src/core/intent/` or this test path; no reconciliation needed.

## Recovered symbols (original → current)

| Original (`80f1d45:src/core/mcp-native.ts`) | Recovered as |
| --- | --- |
| `intent_stale` tool (`sweepStale` from `./intent/ledger.js`) | `intent_stale` → `nativeIntentStale` → current `sweepStale` (`src/core/intent/sweep.ts`) |
| `intent_link` tool (`noteMergedPulls` batch wrapper) | `intent_link` → `nativeIntentLink` → `readLedger` + `linkMergedPull` (`src/core/intent/evidence.ts`) + `writeLedger` (`src/core/intent/store.ts`) |
| `intent_ship` tool (`noteShippedRelease`) | `intent_ship` → `nativeIntentShip` → current `noteShippedRelease` (`src/core/intent/release.ts`) |
| (none — original relied on the tolerant generic validator) | `validNativeEvidence` in `src/core/intent/native-evidence.ts`, wired as a `callNativeTool` dispatch branch before the KILL gate, matching the `phantom_agent_bus_post`/fleet-apps strict-validation pattern |

All three tools are `safety: 'append'` so KILL refuses them before any handler
runs. Handlers lazy-import `./intent/native-evidence.js` inside `mcp-native.ts`,
consistent with current native tools; the module statically imports only the
small local intent modules.

## Files changed (3 code/test paths + this note)

- `src/core/mcp-native.ts` — +29/−1: three `NativeToolImpl` registrations at the
  top of `TOOLS` and one strict-validation dispatch branch.
- `src/core/intent/native-evidence.ts` — NEW, 95 lines: `validNativeEvidence`
  wire-contract validator plus `nativeIntentStale` / `nativeIntentLink` /
  `nativeIntentShip` handlers.
- `test/mcp-native-intent-evidence-09sqn1.test.ts` — NEW, 216 lines: 6 tests
  through the real `listNativeTools` / `nativeToolSafety` / `callNativeTool`
  boundary with `ASHLR_RUNS_DIR` isolated to a mkdtemp root, fake RQ keys and
  fake repo/release values only.

Net LOC: ~340 insertions, 1 deletion across the three code/test files.

## Commands run and actual results

- `git fetch origin master`, `git fetch origin pull/4235/head` — ok;
  `git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD` = `80f1d451949b26685cafa3ffa973d3933901634d`.
- `npm run install:worktree` — ok (pnpm 10.28.2, shared store; healed a partial
  eslint install so lint could run).
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/mcp-native-intent-evidence-09sqn1.test.ts`
  — **PASS, 6/6 tests**, exit 0.
- `node_modules/eslint/bin/eslint.js --no-warn-ignored -- src/core/intent/native-evidence.ts src/core/mcp-native.ts test/mcp-native-intent-evidence-09sqn1.test.ts`
  — **PASS**, exit 0, no findings.
- `npx --no-install tsgo --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` — **PASS**, exit 0, no
  output (verified `node_modules/.bin/tsgo` exists).
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/m31.native-tools.test.ts` — 14/16 pass;
  `exposes the contracted native tools` **FAILS as expected** (see below); one
  unrelated `ashlr_backlog` timeout under load passed on isolated re-run.
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/m31.contract-lock.test.ts` — 5/6 pass;
  `the native tool names and their safety classes are pinned` **FAILS as
  expected** (same additive-surface tripwire).

## Intentional differences from the original

- **Strict argument validation.** The original relied on the generic
  `validateArgs`, which tolerates unknown keys and cannot check array item
  types. `validNativeEvidence` now rejects unknown keys (including any
  caller-supplied `root`/path), enforces required fields and primitive types,
  requires `repo` to match `owner/name`, `number` a safe integer ≥ 1, a
  non-blank `title`, `apply` a real boolean, `release` within
  `MAX_RELEASE_REF`, and each `rq` entry a canonical `RQ-…` key via
  `normalizeRq` (capped at `MAX_RQ`). Invalid calls return the standard
  `Invalid arguments …` isError before the KILL gate and never reach storage.
- **`intent_link` return shape.** Original returned `{ ok, updated }` from the
  batch `noteMergedPulls`. There is no batch wrapper on master, so the handler
  performs the CLI's single-pull `readLedger → linkMergedPull → writeLedger`
  sequence and returns `{ ok, updated, matches: [{ id, status }] }` — a
  superset that lets agents see which directives were touched.
- **`intent_ship` return shape.** Original returned `{ ok, updated }`; current
  `noteShippedRelease` already returns `{ updated, matches }`, preserved
  verbatim.
- **`intent_stale` return shape.** Current `sweepStale` returns
  `{ stale, applied, updated }` (the original had no `updated`); surfaced
  unchanged under `ok: true`.
- **Sweep semantics are the current ones**, per the preservation audit:
  apply re-queues live work and records `propose-superseded`/`await-verification`
  sweep evidence; it never sets `closureProposal`, never closes or supersedes,
  and never dispatches.
- **Descriptions rewritten** to state the caller-supplied-evidence contract
  (no GitHub verification, no publication, no completion claims), matching the
  safety posture of the recovered modules.
- **Tool placement** at the top of `TOOLS`, matching sibling recovery jobs
  (#4491 `intent_import`, #4516 `intent_add`/`intent_update`), which are not on
  master yet; their registrations are preserved untouched if they land first.

## Known follow-ups (not done here, by file-budget constraint)

- **Contract/doc surfaces must be updated additively when the intent tool set
  lands**: `docs/MCP-TOOLS.md` (drives `contractedNativeToolNames` in
  `test/helpers/native-tool-contract.ts`), the pinned list in
  `test/m31.contract-lock.test.ts`, and the same for sibling jobs'
  `intent_import`/`intent_add`/`intent_update`. Until then
  `test/m31.native-tools.test.ts` and `test/m31.contract-lock.test.ts` fail on
  the tool-surface assertions only. This mirrors open PRs #4491/#4516, which
  carry the identical deferred update.
- **Remaining #4235 gaps** (per `docs/intent-preservation-4235.md`): native
  `intent_list`/`intent_get`/`intent_add`/`intent_update`/`intent_import`
  (claimed by sibling jobs), world-model intent projection, the
  `fleet-runs-api` automatic `noteMergedPulls` caller, and batch
  `noteMergedPulls` itself. This subset does not establish complete
  preservation and does not authorize closing #4235.

## Safety notes

- No caller-controlled filesystem root: handlers call the store with its
  default resolution (`ASHLR_RUNS_DIR` or `~/.ashlr-runs`); a `root` argument
  is rejected as an unknown key (tested).
- Link/ship record caller-supplied evidence only — no network, no GitHub
  verification, no publication, no `verified` promotion (terminal statuses are
  preserved; tested).
- Stale preview mutates zero bytes; apply goes through `sweepStale` and never
  claims completion (tested byte-identical preview, post-apply reread).
- Corrupt-store and invalid-argument failures are sanitized isError results —
  store bytes are never echoed (tested).
- KILL (`safety: 'append'`) refuses all three tools before handlers run
  (tested); output scrubbing, the 32 KiB cap and argument-key-only audits are
  the unchanged `callNativeTool` pipeline.
- No commits, pushes, tags or publishes; all changes left uncommitted in the
  worktree.
</details>

# RQ-PHX-RECUTTOPC59: bridge notes

## Chosen PR

**#3640: bridge: RQ-PHX-RELEASEGATESTART05SRQ2.** It adds `ashlr fleet release-gate-start --repo OWNER/REPO --sha FULLSHA [--apply] --json`.

By default the verb only reads and plans. With `--apply` it reads the repo again and then dispatches `ci.yml` with `release_gate=true`. It does that only when all of these hold:
- the given SHA is the default-branch head, checked on two separate reads;
- the `ci.yml` run inventory for that SHA came back as one complete page (not truncated);
- no `workflow_dispatch` or `schedule` gate run is already in flight.

Moved heads, partial or failed inventory, unknown run statuses and dispatch failures are all refused, with bounded and scrubbed error detail. This is gates work.

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-PHX-INTENTBATCHRECOVER09SQL1

## Summary

Recovered the missing `noteMergedPulls` persistence API from retained PR #4235
(original commit `80f1d451949b26685cafa3ffa973d3933901634d`) into the current
intent ledger module, per the Nov 5 21:46 order to preserve every original
unique PR capability.

- `src/core/intent/merge-batch.ts` (new, 90 lines): `noteMergedPulls(pulls,
  { root, now })` reads the ledger via `readLedger`, links each valid pull
  through the existing pure `linkMergedPull` matcher, and writes once via
  `writeLedger`. Returns `{ updated }` = count of distinct directives matched
  (original unique-directive semantics).
- `src/core/intent/ledger.ts`: one re-export line adding `noteMergedPulls` plus
  its option/result types.
- `test/intent-merge-batch-recovery-09sql1.test.ts` (new, 150 lines): 6 tests
  against real temporary-root disk persistence and rereads.

## Behavior preserved from the original

- Empty ledger → `{ updated: 0 }` with no file write.
- Invalid `repo` pulls are skipped; a pull with an invalid `number` throws
  (`EvidenceError`, same message) and a failed batch never writes, so no
  partially recorded batch persists.
- Batch timestamp is `opts.now ?? now` applied to every pull (a pull's own
  `at` is ignored inside a batch, as in the original `nowIso(opts.now)`).
- Two PRs matching the same directive persist both `prs` entries and count
  the directive once; unmatched directives are untouched; shipped/verified/
  closed/superseded statuses are never regressed (delegated to
  `linkMergedPull`'s `OPEN_FOR_MERGE` promotion).

## Deliberate safety-compatible differences (documented in module header)

- Replays are idempotent: a pull whose matched directives already carry its
  `repo#number` `pr` evidence row is skipped, and on partial overlap the
  duplicate evidence row is removed after linking. The original re-appended
  duplicate evidence rows on every call.
- The ledger is written only when a pull actually changed an item (the
  original rewrote whenever `updated > 0`, even for pure replays).
- Non-array `pulls` throws `IntentError` instead of a `TypeError`.

## Commands run

- `git fetch origin pull/4235/head`; `git show 80f1d451…:src/core/intent/ledger.ts`
  and `:test/intent-ledger.test.ts` (source of truth for behavior).

  — 6/6 passed.
